correctness.rationale: For two distinct rates 0<a<b and interior weight, re-derived (log f)"/d^2=-(alpha-1)/t^2+1/[4cosh^2((t-log r)/2)] with d=b-a>0,t=dx,r=wb^alpha/((1-w)a^alpha). For alpha<=1 the curvature is strictly positive on x>0; for alpha>1 strict log-concavity of log H_c(t) where H_c=t/[2cosh((t-c)/2)] yields unique maximum. Its maximum strictly increases with c via H_{c+h}(t+h)=(t+h)/t H_c(t). At sharp tangency derivative zero and curvature zero imply t=2sqrt(alpha) and c*=2sqrt(alpha)+log((sqrt(alpha)-1)/(sqrt(alpha)+1)). Strict log-H concavity classifies one bounded positive-curvature interval above threshold, isolated equality at threshold. Confirmed tangency and curvature signs independently for five shapes; full proof analytic for all real parameters.
residual_risks: At r=R_alpha curvature zero at one x but ordinary log-concavity (nonpositive second derivative) still holds.
At coincident rates or a pure component the single-Gamma classification alpha>=1 differs from the distinct-rate alpha>1 theorem; exclusions are explicit.

value.rationale: A complete necessary-sufficient inequality for the simplest genuinely heterogeneous rate Gamma mixture gives a sharp normalized weight independent of rate gap, complete curvature sign topology and non-closedness of global log-concavity under arbitrarily small rate heterogeneity in total variation. This is a natural reliability/phase-type mixture classification rather than arbitrary parameter fitting.
residual_risks: Value rests on the specific natural mathematical invariant and nontrivial sharp classification; no general theorem beyond stated scope is claimed.

limitations: Exactly two distinct rates with common positive real shape and strictly interior mixture weight; excludes >=3 components, unequal shapes and general mixing measures.
